Thanks Ben — technical details below. I captured the typical fields and the export mechanics so HelixCare can validate against their control matrix. 

What we log (admin activity / operator ledger) — representative fields:
- event_id (UUID)
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- tenant_id / account_id
- actor_id (user id or service principal)
- actor_email (if available)
- event_type (e.g., ADMIN_CONSOLE_LOGIN, API_KEY_CREATE, ROLE_GRANT, MODEL_DEPLOY, TOKEN_REVOKE)
- target_resource (resource id and type)
- change_delta (pre/post JSON blob for config changes; null for auth events)
- source_ip, user_agent
- request_id / correlation_id
- geo (country, region derived from IP)
- outcome (SUCCESS | FAILURE)
- retention_class (hot | cold)

Retention & availability:
- Default: 90 days hot (queryable in console), archived to cold storage for 1 year total by default.
- Extended retention: customers can request 3y / 7y retention packages (legal/contract required).
- For SOC 2 evidence packages we typically produce a timeboxed snapshot and a manifest; retained evidence can also be exported to the customer’s S3 (if approved).

Export formats and packaging:
- Preferred formats: gzipped JSONL (readable, preserves nested change_delta), Parquet (columnar, smaller for analytics), CSV (flat fields only).
- Packaging: bundle the exported files in a tar.gz, include a manifest JSON that lists file names, SHA256 checksums, record counts, and export-timestamp. Example manifest filename: admin_activity_snapshot_2028-03-28.manifest.json
- Signing: manifest is signed with Redwood KMS (detached signature) and we include chain-of-custody notes in README.

Delivery options:
- Presigned S3 PUT for Redwood to upload (preferred). S3 link + expiry window provided.
- SFTP to customer endpoint (secure, non-cloud customers).
- Direct transfer to a customer-managed bucket via role-assume cross-account replication (requires IAM setup).

PII and redaction:
- We can hash/email-mask actor_email or remove free-text fields on request. Note: removing change_delta may reduce auditability — recommend hashed actor_email + retained actor_id mapping in separate mapping file delivered under DPA if required.

Sampling and scope:
- We recommend a 7-day sample (first deliverable) to confirm schema. Once schema is validated we will run the full snapshot for the requested scope date.

Costs & lead times:
- Sample: no charge. Full snapshot export: operational fee for >50GB exports; quoted after scope confirmation.
- Lead time: sample within 24h; full snapshot within 48h after export approval and signed export terms.

I’ll generate a sample schema file and README and attach it to the presigned link for your reviewers.

— Olga Petrov

Julia / Ben — a couple legal points to keep in mind before we transfer: 

- Export Authorization: we need signed export authorization from HelixCare (simple one-paragraph approval listing the target account IDs and delivery mechanism).
- DPA & Data Minimization: if HelixCare requires PII redaction, please confirm scope and whether Redwood should maintain a mapping key (we can provide a hashed mapping under a separate, DPA-limited artifact).
- On-prem / air-gapped transfers: these require 7 business days to route approvals and additional verification steps.
- SLA & retention amendments: any changes to default retention must be added as an addendum to the contract or a short SOW.

I’ll prepare a short draft export authorization and the minimal terms we need for the one-off snapshot. Ben — if you can confirm the account IDs and the target transfer option, I’ll circulate the doc for signature.
